x: Jim Heathfield was second in the 440 and Terry Bateman won the high jump. Tea and sandwiches were provided afterwards by our hosts, prominent among whom were our old friends Syd Jarlett and Bill Speaight..
Jeffery reaping the reward of his perseverance by being placed second and Sid Jarlett who has now gone over to walking, securing third place.

However, nine of our walkers turned out and, considering that Surrey Walking Club were out in fairly good strength, gave a good account of themselves. Syd James was first home, in 3rd place, with Syd Jarlett 6th and George Oliver 9th. Scoring 9 a side, Surrey won by 65 points to 106.
In the 2 miles walk George Oliver made good use of his long mark to win in very fast time with young E. Hall second and our old friend Sid Jarlett in third place.

Oliver and Syd Jarlett once again gaining the minor placings The 220 Yards handicap saw the scratch man Don Merrett run through his field in easy fashion to record 22.8 and he should be up with the best next season on the track.
Syd Jarlett is improving steadily and will soon be among the leading walkers. This is no idle prophecy and we expect Syd to be quite an asset to our Junior teams later on.
Among the new members of the section to distinguish themselves were Jim Tebbutt, Hugh McGreechan, Syd Jarlett and George Checkley, who all look set for successful walking careers.
Hall, who is quite a promising youngster, finished second, with Syd Jarlett holding off Harry Shields down the straight to take third place.

At this point Belgrave were lying 6th but our whips got busy and got Syd Jarlett, George Checkley and Gordon Waddingham together in 19th, 20th and 21st positions, with Hugh McGreechan just behind in 25th place, at 8 miles, which brought our team to 3rd place.

George Checkley and Syd Jarlett walked extremely well. Our President was on the spot on our arrival with a coat stand to complete the dressing room and we were further supported by Gordon Waddingham, Joe Coleman and Percy Wilson, the latter, as usual, managing to find a bike within a few minutes of his arrival.
Hall with Syd Jarlett second and A. Wesson third, while first prize in the Javelin Throw went to a junior member in R.

Early in the race, Syd Jarlett, although suffering from a very heavy cold was leading our team in the 12th position. Then came Ron Kemp closely followed by five others with Alan Robins starting steadily in the rear.
Eddie Short ran 2nd in the 2 miles steeplechase while Harry Churcher once again won the 2 miles walk with Syd Jarlett doing well to take 3rd position.
The 3 mile walk was won by S. Jarlett who had too much in hand for Ray Middleton (off 1.50).

When they came in sight of the finish Bill Lucas was clear away in front and in 2nd position came Len Marchant, a fine performance by both runners. 1, W.Lucas 26:55; 2, L.Marchant 27:03; 15, S.Jarlett 27:55; 23, L.Bishop 28:16. Teams: 1, Belgrave H 41; 2, Herne Hill 48.
